title: Replace Writer's Bespoke Jack Lexer/Parser With Shared Trinity Jack Parser
description: D1: writer/plugin/rs/lib.rs hand-rolls its own Jack-language lexer (JackLexKind/JackLexToken/tokenize_jack_source), recursive-descent parser (JackAstParser) and span-tracked AST (JackAstNode) purely to power its outline/tree panel, hover, newline-gating, placeholder, rename and symbol-at-cursor editor features. trinity_jack (trinity/jack/core/rs/lib.rs) already implements the same Cypher-inspired Jack grammar (MATCH/WHERE/RETURN/CREATE/DELETE/SET/MERGE) as the canonical parser, but only exposes a semantic (unspanned) Query AST via parse() plus a coarse tokenize() for syntax highlighting -- neither is granular/spanned enough for writer's tree panel or fine-grained editor heuristics. Task: delete writer's local lexer/parser/AST entirely; additively extend trinity_jack's public API (expose its internal fine-grained spanned token lexer, and add a new spanned/tree AST entry point) so writer can route all of its Jack lexing/parsing through trinity_jack, keeping only its own presentation-layer (tree-item id/icon mapping) code. Preserve writer's existing behavior/tests exactly.
summary:
Deleted writer's hand-rolled Jack lexer/parser/AST (JackLexKind, JackLexToken, tokenize_jack_source, JackAstParser, and the jack_ast_node/collapse_whitespace builder helpers -- ~530 lines) and routed all of writer's Jack-language handling through trinity_jack.

trinity_jack extension (additive only, no existing pub API shape/behavior changed):
- Widened visibility of the existing internal fine-grained lexer: `enum Token` and `struct SpannedToken` (with its fields) are now `pub`, and `fn lex_spanned(input, forgiving)` (unchanged signature/behavior) is now `pub fn`. This is the same lexer trinity_jack's own `parse`/`tokenize` already used internally -- no new lexing logic, just exposed.
- Added a new `#region 🔖SpannedAst` (between the existing Parser and Executor regions) with `pub struct SpannedNode { kind, label, start, end, children }` and `pub fn parse_spanned(source: &str) -> SpannedNode`, ported 1:1 from writer's former JackAstParser (same grammar, same node "kind" strings: query/match/where/return/create/delete/set/merge/pattern/patternNode/edge/edgeVar/edgeKind/var/label/property/returnItem/assignment/or/and/eq/ne/number/string/bool/null/error), just rebuilt on trinity_jack's own Token/SpannedToken instead of a duplicate token type. Lexing uses `forgiving=true` (never fails, matching the old tokenizer's guarantee for live-typing editors); only the recursive-descent parse step can fail, producing a single "error" node spanning the source, exactly as before.
- Added 4 tests to trinity_jack's existing `🧪Tests` module covering `lex_spanned` forgiving-mode and `parse_spanned` shape/error-node behavior.

writer/plugin/rs/lib.rs:
- `JackAstNode` (writer's own presentation-layer struct with the tree-item `id`) is kept, but is now built via a 12-line `jack_ast_from_spanned()` adapter over `trinity_jack::SpannedNode` instead of being constructed inline by a local parser. `parse_jack_ast()` is now one line: `jack_ast_from_spanned(&trinity_jack::parse_spanned(text))`. All downstream consumers (find_deepest_jack_ast_node_at, jack_ast_node_by_id, jack_ast_node_for_selection, jack_ast_to_tree_item) are untouched.
- The fine-grained-token editor heuristics (jack_editor_placeholders, jack_newline_allowed_at/jack_newline_gate_offsets, jack_bound_variable_names, jack_variable_occurrences, jack_symbol_at_offset, plus the JACK_NEWLINE_AFTER_KEYWORDS table) were rewritten against `trinity_jack::{Token, SpannedToken}` via a new `jack_tokens()` helper (`trinity_jack::lex_spanned(text, true)`), replacing the old `tokenize_jack_source`/`JackLexKind`/`JackLexToken`. Same never-fails guarantee, same logic, only the token type changed (Ident/Number/StringLit now carry their text inside the enum variant instead of a separate `.text` field).

Behavior reconciliation: none needed -- trinity_jack's forgiving lexer is byte-for-byte equivalent to writer's former hand-rolled lexer (same character classes, same keyword table, same negative-number/arrow/unterminated-string handling), and the new parse_spanned parser is a direct structural port of writer's former JackAstParser (same grammar, same node kinds/labels/spans, same single-"error"-node failure mode). No app-observable behavior change.

Verified: rustfmt --check on both touched files, comparing before/after diff counts to confirm zero *new* formatting violations were introduced (all remaining diffs are pre-existing drift in code I did not touch, same content just at shifted line numbers). Exhaustive grep cross-reference confirms zero remaining references to JackLexKind/JackLexToken/tokenize_jack_source/JackAstParser/collapse_whitespace/jack_ast_node(. Brace balance check on both files (0/0). Manually desk-checked every match-ergonomics/ownership site introduced by switching from Copy JackLexKind to non-Copy trinity_jack::Token (all matches are non-binding discriminant checks or ref-pattern binds, no move errors). Confirmed trinity_jack's other consumers (trinity/plugin, trinity/jack/lsp, trinity/jack/shell, trinity/rewrite/engine) only use explicit named imports (no glob imports), so the new/widened pub items cannot collide -- change is purely additive/backward compatible for them.

NOT verified (left for the orchestrator's final gate): `cargo check -p trinity_jack` / `cargo check -p writer-plugin` did not return output after several minutes (background job left running) -- consistent with the documented heavy concurrent cargo-lock contention from other active sessions; did not run `cargo test` for the same reason. No genuine correctness bugs found beyond the migration itself.

Nothing needed to be flagged as inexpressible with existing primitives -- trinity_jack's existing lexer internals were already exactly what writer needed once exposed, so no awkward workaround was required.
